tagline.text: A walk-through hillside zoo in Rizal focused on native Philippine wildlife

location.label: Location
location.text: Sitio Gulod, San Isidro, Rodriguez (Montalban), Rizal

best_season.label: Best time to visit
best_season.text: November–May dry season (early morning visits recommended)

duration.label: Time needed
duration.text: Half day to full day (3–5 hours)

budget.label: Budget
budget.text: About ₱1,100~1,500 (per person, day trip including transport, admission and snacks)

children.text: Avilon Zoo is a non-profit zoo on a hillside of about 7.5 hectares in Rodriguez (Montalban), Rizal, where you walk among more than 3,000 animals of over 600 species. Known for breeding and conserving native Philippine wildlife, it makes an easy day trip from Metro Manila.

Avilon Zoo is located in the barangay of San Isidro in Rodriguez, Rizal (formerly known as Montalban). It is run by the non-profit Avilon Wildlife Conservation Foundation, covers about 7.5 hectares, and opened in 2005 according to Wikipedia. There are no amusement rides; it is a purely walk-through zoo where you follow paths along the hillside and meet the animals one after another.

The collection holds more than 3,000 animals of over 600 species, including mammals, birds, reptiles, amphibians, freshwater fish and invertebrates. The zoo is known for keeping and breeding endemic and native Philippine species in particular. A well-known example is the butaan (Gray's monitor), a giant monitor lizard found only in the Philippines. The zoo is reported to have succeeded in hatching and raising the species in captivity, and the story has been featured in an animal documentary. It is also a member of the Southeast Asian Zoos Association (SEAZA).

The route has numbered markers and leads past the arapaima pond, the orangutan pavilion, reptile caves, walk-in aviaries, a giraffe deck and a tortoise patio. Some animals can be fed, which makes the zoo a good choice for children. Most of the inner route goes up and down slopes and involves quite a lot of walking, so comfortable shoes are a good idea.

It lies close to the northeastern edge of Metro Manila, so it is an easy day trip from Quezon City or Marikina. By public transport, however, you change between jeepneys or vans and finish with a tricycle ride, so leave plenty of time. Prices and opening hours differ slightly between sources, so it is safest to check the official website or call before you go. This is a long-loved family outing, but reviews are divided on the animals' living conditions, so judge the facilities for yourself. With children, try talking about each animal's habitat and conservation as you walk. Basing yourself around Cubao or Marikina shortens the trip.
You can see the arapaima, one of the largest freshwater fish in the world, up close. The area is known for feeding experiences, and children especially love it.

This popular area houses Bornean orangutans. Visitor reviews often mention the orangutans by name, and a photo experience is sometimes offered, so check the on-site notices. Orangutans are most active during the day, so it is best to see them first thing in the morning.

Keeping mainly Philippine native animals is the hallmark of this zoo. Through species such as the Philippine falconet and the Samar cobra, and the butaan breeding story, you can learn about Philippine ecology and conservation in an easy way. Take your time to read the information boards as you walk.
You can observe snakes, lizards and turtles in dark, cave-style exhibits. It is a cool place to stop and escape the midday heat.
You can walk inside the aviaries and see the birds close up. If you walk quietly without making loud noises, you will spot more birds.
Look down from the deck at large herbivores such as giraffes and zebras. Reviews also mention hippos, a spotted hyena, meerkats, warthogs and sun bears.

Watch the large tortoises move at their leisurely pace. You can buy a feeding cup and feed waterfowl, tortoises, deer and other animals. With children, choosing just one or two activities keeps the cost and time manageable.

items.title: Public transport day trip
items.subtitle: A day trip starting from Cubao

children.text: Exit the LRT-2 Araneta Center-Cubao station by the south exit and take a jeepney, FX or van bound for Montalban from the stops along Aurora Boulevard or near Farmers Market. Tell the driver you want to get off at Eastwood Greenview.
Get off at the entrance of Eastwood Greenview (near the gas station and the market) and take a tricycle to the zoo gate. There is a tricycle terminal just outside the gate.
After entering, follow the numbered markers and work your way down from the highest area. See the outdoor areas first, before the heat builds.
Have a light lunch at the on-site canteen and rest in the shade. Outside food carries a corkage fee.
Enjoy the shaded areas such as the reptile caves and aviaries, try a feeding experience and browse the souvenir shop.
Take a tricycle from the gate to the main road, then board a jeepney or van back to Manila. Leave early to avoid the rush-hour traffic.
Many reviewers say the trip takes about
1 hour 30 minutes–2 hours
one way because of traffic and transfers. On weekends, check the last entry and closing times in advance.

items.title: Half-day trip by car
items.subtitle: Easy by taxi or private car

children.text: Arrive at opening time. Parking is reported to be free for private cars.
See the orangutan pavilion and the giraffe deck first, while it is quiet just after opening.
When the sun gets strong, move on to the aviaries and the reptile caves.
Have lunch on site and buy souvenirs.
Leave before the crowds grow and head back.
Reviewers say a taxi from Cubao takes about
25 minutes
when traffic is light, but it takes much longer during weekday rush hours.
Exit the LRT-2 Araneta Center-Cubao station by the south exit and take a jeepney, FX or UV van bound for Montalban (Rodriguez) from Aurora Boulevard or near Farmers Market.
The drop-off point is Eastwood Greenview Subdivision (near the gas station and the market). Tell the driver you are going to Avilon Zoo and he will let you know.
From there, take a tricycle to the zoo gate. Reviewers mention jeepney or FX fares of about
and about
for the tricycle, but fares may have increased.
On the way back, take a tricycle from the terminal outside the gate to the main road, then board a jeepney or van bound for Manila. Vehicles become scarce in the late afternoon, so leave before dark.
From central Manila it usually takes about
1 hour 30 minutes–2 hours
. Jeepneys and vans also run in the same direction from Quezon City and Marikina.
It is about
20km
from Cubao. You can use a taxi, Grab or a rental car.
Part of the road is mountainous and traffic is heavy, so avoid rush hours. It can be hard to find a ride back, so plan ahead.
Drivers of private cars are reported to be able to use the zoo parking lot for free.
From Ninoy Aquino International Airport (MNL), travel through Manila to Cubao, then transfer to a Montalban-bound vehicle.
With a lot of luggage you can take a taxi or Grab straight from the airport, but the distance is long and the fare is high.
Because this is an outdoor walking zoo, the weather matters a great deal. The dry season from November to May is comfortable for walking, and December to February is relatively cool.
Many reviews say the best time of day is just after opening, between 8:00 and 10:00 in the morning. The sun gets strong and crowds grow later in the day. Weekdays are quieter than weekends.

children.text: Prices are approximate as of
and may vary with local conditions.
Inside the zoo there is a canteen and a snack stand serving simple meals, and reviewers say a meal costs about

. Outside food is reported to carry a corkage fee, so check the notices on site. Food for the animals may not be brought in. Water and snacks are sold at the stand, but prices may be higher than in the city, so it is better to bring plenty of water.

Most visitors stay in Manila, Quezon City, Marikina or Antipolo and make the trip in a day. There are small guesthouses and resorts around Montalban, but information is limited, so check the location and reviews before booking. Near the entrance of Eastwood Greenview there are a market and small eateries where you can grab a bite on the way back.
Arrive at opening time (8:00 on weekdays). From about 10:00 the heat climbs quickly and the crowds grow.
Online tickets are often cheaper than buying at the gate, so check the official website or a booking site before you go. Senior and PWD discounts are said not to apply to online tickets.
There are few ATMs nearby and the mobile signal can be weak, so carry enough cash in small bills and save your booking confirmation offline.
Wear non-slip sneakers; dirt paths get slippery in the rainy season. Bring insect repellent and about 2 liters of water per adult.
Plan 3 to 5 hours and treat it as a full-day outing. Strollers and wheelchairs are reportedly available for rent on site, but the many hills can make them hard to use.
Feed animals only in the designated areas and only with the official feeding cups. Do not give them your own food.

If you are going for the first time from Metro Manila, set Eastwood Greenview Subdivision as your destination in Google Maps. Asking the driver or fellow passengers to tell you where to get off is safer.
Admission fees and opening hours differ between sources and may change, so check the latest announcements on the official website or by phone before your visit.

According to the official FAQ, pets, alcoholic drinks, drones, bikes and scooters may not be brought in, and smoking (including vaping) is not allowed. Children aged 12 and under are reported to need to enter with a paying adult.
Do not put your fingers through the fences or climb over barriers. Wild animals are unpredictable and can bite or injure you.
The grounds are hilly, so seniors and small children should pace themselves. Paths become slippery when it rains.
There are many transfers on public transport, so it is safer to head back before dark. Keep valuables on your person.
Opinions on animal welfare and conservation vary among visitors. Check the facilities and the animals' conditions yourself when you visit, and do not do anything that startles the animals.
A city known for its pilgrimage church and scenic viewpoints, about
1 hour
away by car. Rather than combining it with the zoo on the same day, it is more relaxing to make it a separate outing.
An urban nature park in Quezon City, good for an easy walk and a look at the gardens.
The center of the Philippine shoe industry, where you can see a shoe museum and workshops. It is a good stop on the way back to Manila.

A limestone nature conservation area in Rizal, visited by advance reservation and following the guides' instructions. It makes a good separate trip for those who want more nature experiences; check the latest operating information.
An old public zoo in central Manila that is easy to tour within the city. The size and atmosphere are different, so comparing the two can be interesting.
